pages.text: Of some of them, almost nothing is left. This one drifted through the mist in a ragged hood, and when it stopped, it knelt, as if it still remembered how to pray. It attacked me with light that burned like poison. When it fell, it did not scream. It sighed, the way you sigh when you finally put down something heavy. What was it praying for, all this time? Did it pray to go home, or did it pray to stay? I cannot get the sound of that sigh out of my head. I wonder which of the two I would pray for, if I knelt like that.
